correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge2\), \(\left\{{j\atop2}\right\}=2^{j-1}-1\) and the unsigned Stirling generating identity give exactly \(P_{n,2}(z)=(R_n(2z)-2R_n(z))/(n!(n-1))\). For every nonzero \(z\) with \(\operatorname{Re}z\ge0\), each integer \(1\le h\le n-1\) has \(|2z+h|^2-|z+h|^2=3|z|^2+2h\operatorname{Re}z>0\). Hence the corresponding products have unequal moduli and cannot cancel. The positive \(z^2\) coefficient \(\left[{n\atop2}\right]/L(n,2)\) proves exactly double zero at the origin. The \(n=2\) quotient is constant. Code at the actual embedded path verifies 79 finite coefficient cases and a degree-eight nonreal-root witness, not infinity; the analytic product proof establishes the universal assertion.

Targeted published-finding corpus and literature comparisons using naming, algebraic equivalents, and stronger-coverage aliases returned no covering statement. These checks support originality but cannot certify unique priority.

value.rationale: Two blocks is the first nontrivial Lah block count after the permutation-cycle k=1 case and gives an unbounded all-n subfamily of the explicit original zero-location conjecture (arXiv:2105.11365v2, Conjecture 3.11). At n=8 the polynomial already contains genuinely nonreal zeros, demonstrating a location question not answered by all-real-root techniques. Strict Hurwitz stability for the whole subfamily informs probability generating-function methodology and is not implied by the known selected integer roots or log-concavity. No claims for k>=3, r>0 or new CLTs are made.
